texts.facts: The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Udayveer Balmiki suffered grievous injury and amputation of left lower limb. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/petitioner. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 09.01.2021 at about 05:30 p.m., petitioner/injured Udayveer Balmiki was travelling on his motorcycle number UP-81BJ-5840 from Agra to Kuverpur Chauraha, at a normal speed according to traffic rules. At about 03:00 p.m. when he reached Reliance Petrol Pump, Ghhalesar, a TSR (Chhota Hathi) bearing no.UP-83BT-7724 (hereafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came at a high speed from behind and hit the motorcycle which petitioner was riding. Due to the impact, petitioner fell and sustained grievous injury. He was removed to S.S. Hospital, Agra where his MLC was prepared. Thereafter on 11.01.2021, he was referred to Pushpanjali Hospital, Agra. He was further referred to JPN Apex Trauma Center AIIMS, New Delhi for treatment where he was operated and his left leg above knee was amputed. He was discharged from hospital on 04.02.2021 and thereafter continued to take treatment as an outdoor patient. 3. An FIR no.0029/21, dated 24.01.2021 was registered u/s 279/338 of IPC, PS Atmadpur, Agra, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned CHARU GUPTA Date: 2025.07.30 MACT No. 837/21 Uday Veer Balmiki vs. Shailender Singh & ors. P.No..2 of 24 BK criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3/TATA AIG General Insurance is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Written statement was not filed by respondent no. 1 and 2 despite opportunity. In its reply, respondent no.3 has assailed the territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal and also denied its liability on the ground that there is an unexplained delay of 15 days in lodging of the FIR, raising a doubt in the veracity of the claim. It is further pleaded that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner. Respondent no.3 has further denied its liability to indemnify the insured /respondent no.2 or compensate the petitioner in case respondents were found to be in breach of the insurance policy. 6. Vide order dated 02.02.2024, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 09.01.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-81BJ-5840 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Udayveer Balmiki led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testifies on the CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.30 17:25:58 +0530 MACT No. 837/21 Uday Veer Balmiki vs. Shailender Singh & ors. P.No.3 of 24 BK lines of the claim petition and deposed that on 09.01.2021 at about 3 p.m. he went from Agra to Kuverpur Chauraha on his motor cycle no. UP-81BJ-5840 in a normal speed by obeying the traffic rules and regulations on his correct side. When PW-1 reached at Reliance Petrol Pump, Ghhalesar, the offending vehicle came from the back side which was driving by respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner. Due to this impact, he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. PW-1 was taken to S.S. Hospital, Agra and his MLC was prepared. On 11.01.2021 PW-1 was referred to Pushpanjali Hospital, Agra. On 11.01.2021 PW-1 was again referred to JPN Apex Trauma Centre, AIIMS Hospital, New Delhi. During the treatment he was operated and his left leg above knee amputated and discharged on 04.02.2021. PW-1 further deposed that he was doing private job as a Field Executive and was earning Rs.18,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month. He deposed that he has so far incurred Rs.2 lac on medical treatment and Rs.4,35,750/- incurred on artificial limb as per estimate from Ottobock Health Care. He relied upon driving licence as Mark A, medical treatment document as Ex.PW1/1, Medical bills as Mark B, disability certificate as Ex.PW1/2, estimate bill of artificial limb issued by Fusion Rehab Innovation Clinic as Ex.PW1/3, Adhar card and PAN card of petitioner as Ex.PW-1/4 and criminal record documents as Ex.PW1/5. He was duly cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. PW-2 Ms. Sakshi, Counsellor from Ottobock Health Care CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 17:26:07 Shailender Singh & ors. P.No..4 of 24 BK Pvt.Ltd., South Patel Nagar, deposed that she had brought the authority letter enclosed with her ID card as Ex.PW2/1 and RSP (Rehabilitation Service Proposal) along with cover letter Ex.PW2/2 of injured namely Uday Veer Balmiki, s/o Sh. Jhumman Lal Balmiki aged about 49 years, r/o Moh. Imliwala, Namaj Pada Atrauli, Aligarh, U.P.-202280. PW-2 was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company. No evidence was led on behalf of the respondents. Uday Veer Balmiki vs Shailender Singh on 30 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153502357/ 3 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company.

Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 16. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. P.No.9 of 24 BK (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
